name: Hohlstamm
prior: Didgeridoo synthesis exists but not as a touch drone with mouth under the finger: Quilcom SIM-DIDGE (free Windows VST, 'synthesis methods only', optional vocal input; VS: plugins4free.com/plugin/3663), Didgeridrone (123creative, Windows effect that turns any input into a didge drone; VS: kvraudio didgeridrone), Soundiron Didgeridoos and UVI World Suite (samples; VS: soundiron.com, gearspace 1252390), didgmo (geometry -> sound predictor for builders; VS: didgmo.sourceforge.net). The KVR thread 'physical modelling of a didgeridoo' has no finished solution (VS: kvraudio viewtopic p=3107734); SOS's wah + feedback-delay experiment 'does not sound like the real instrument' (VS: soundonsound.com/node/4925521); Princeton COS325 notes argue the vocal tract matters more than the bore and point to STK Brass + formant filters (VS: cs.princeton.edu BBFProp.txt); Scavone's lip-reed/mass-spring model (VS: ccrma icmc2002a); Rippler/RipplerX have open/closed tube resonators without a lip (VS: dubspot refx-rippler-2026); Elastic OSC = Plaits on iOS, no didge (VS: apps.apple.com elastic-osc). Myzel: Tiefe is osc + tanh, Halm (inventor) is a flute/clarinet in a worklet. Rare: the lip-valve didge with mouth formants is standard STK/CCRMA territory, but no touch instrument found.
costNotes: All stages are native nodes (ConstantSource mouth, gain -0.85, sum, BQ lip, gain, WaveShaper x^2, two multiplier gains with signal on .gain, DC-block BQ, DelayNode, BQ bore, 1-2 peaking BQ, out, pitchMod->delayTime gain) ~17 nodes with 5-6 biquads + delay -> ~0.7 (idea 0.65 ok), L3 two bores ~1.3; the cycle is legal because it contains a DelayNode, and 2/f at 40-180 Hz = 533-2400 frames >= the 128-frame minimum (R: webaudio.md section 7). A worklet version (waveguide class 0.24 + node/params ~0.15) would cost ~0.35-0.4 and is the better home. 'Hard' is not about CPU: the STK Brass valve as written (V: stk_Brass.h tick: lip two-pole gain 0.03, area = clamp(lip^2), delay = 2 SR/f + 3) has a knife-edge operating window. Measured (M: sim/eng_hst_sim3-5.js, exact STK tick, 120-point grid of lip gain x pressure per pitch): with STK's lip radius 0.997 nothing oscillates at 50 Hz, 7/120 combos at 80 Hz, 12/120 at 110 Hz, 24/120 at 300 Hz; with STK's fixed gain 0.03 the valve is saturated (area = 1 for 100 % of samples) at every pitch tested, so it is silent; the working lip gain scales ~1/f^2 (3e-5 at 50 Hz, 1e-4 at 110, 1.8e-3 at 300) and a narrower lip resonance (radius 0.9995) widens the window to 15/120 at 50 Hz. The oscillation sits 4-13 % sharp of f (lip resonance pulls the pitch), i.e. a per-pitch tuning table for both delay and lip gain is mandatory, and 'vel = Mundruck' walks straight out of the window (press 0.3-0.5 dead, 0.8-1.7 speaks, 2.2 saturated at 110 Hz).
soundHeld: If calibrated it is the only self-excited drone in Myzel and the character is real: a buzzing lip tone with a strong odd/even mix, mouth formants on top that speak when Hoehe moves, Bebung as throat vibrato via the delay. But the sim says the speaking range of the STK valve is narrow in pressure and gain and shifts with pitch, onset is 50-200 ms even in the good region, and the 3rd-mode overblow (lip at 3f) did not oscillate in the grid without its own recalibration - the register jump the idea promises needs a second table. Mouth formants as post-filters on the drone are a wah, not a coupled tract (the SOS finding); it still reads as 'didge' because the lip buzz is right, but the vocalisation is thinner than a real player's. 40-60 Hz is inaudible on phone speakers (formants carry, as the idea says), and the fold to 40-180 Hz means every scale collapses into one register - a Tiefe-like bass that only speaks. Pitch glide (setF) moves delayTime and the lip resonance together; with a-rate delayTime it is smooth, but the valve can drop out mid-glide where the window closes.
soundBurst: Does not work as a Puls hit at bass pitches: with a 220 ms gate the best-case burst RMS was 0.01-0.04 at 80-180 Hz against 0.1-0.3 in steady state (M), i.e. a tongue click plus a faint thump; the idea's 'Druckpuls + 2 ms Klick' is honest about this but then the lane engine is a click, not a drone. Only above ~300 Hz does a 220 ms gate speak (0.21 RMS), which is outside the folded range. Didgeridoo rhythm in Myzel's Puls would have to come from gating the mouth formants/level of a continuously running loop, i.e. a sustaining voice with a lane-driven mouth, which the current Puls model (one voice per hit) does not offer.
failureModes: STK valve operating window: 0-25 % of the gain x pressure grid oscillates; fixed gain 0.03 is silent (saturated) at every pitch; needs per-pitch lip gain ~1/f^2 and pressure clamp (M).
Pitch 4-13 % sharp of the bore tuning; per-octave (better per-semitone) tuning table for delay AND lip gain, offline-calibrated.
Overblow (lip at 3f) needs its own calibration; otherwise Hoehe > 0.8 kills the tone instead of jumping.
Puls bursts <= 220 ms are clicks at 50-180 Hz; no drone per hit.
vel = pressure is the instability axis; low vel = silence, high vel = saturated buzz.
Mouth formants as output filters = wah on a drone, not a coupled tract.
Native cycle: three filter phases + delay interpolation shift the tuning; k-rate parameter changes inside the loop can click (shaper curve swaps).
40-180 Hz fold: one register only, inaudible on phone speakers without the formants.
verdict: Rare: lip-valve + bore + formants is textbook STK/CCRMA and exists as SIM-DIDGE and Didgeridrone on Windows, but no touch instrument found puts the mouth under the finger. The native plan is legal (DelayNode cycle, 533-2400 frames) and cheap (~0.7), yet the sim of the exact STK Brass tick shows the valve speaks in only 0-25 % of the gain x pressure grid, is silent with STK's own gain, sits 4-13 % sharp and gives a click, not a tone, for 220 ms Puls gates at bass pitches - so 'hard': it needs offline calibration tables per pitch for delay, lip gain and pressure, a separate overblow table, and preferably a worklet with a tamer valve (offset/mass-spring lip) instead of x^2-clamp. Worth it only as a held drone engine with the Puls role declared as 'tongue clicks'; if the build budget allows one calibrated self-excited engine, Halm (reed) already measured a wider window.
